cases.name: Ena Cordt
cases.narrative: Sells worked at a Forsyth carnival, where he met her and her 4-year-old son Rory. (According to Sells) Ena invited Sells to her home that evening. According to Sells, he had sex with her, fell asleep, and awoke to find her stealing from his backpack. He proceeded to beat Cordt to death with her son's baseball bat. He then murdered her son because the child was a potential witness. On 7/29/1985, their bodies were found, by which time Sells had left town.

cases.name: Jacqueline L. Brown-Steinert
cases.about: She was a former nurse. Her daughter Nicole Maggard said her mom was caring, honest, funny and giving."She was a healer and a helper," Maggard said. Steinert loved children, especially her grandchildren, and had an infectious laugh, according to her daughter. Before a car crash left her with debilitating injuries several years ago, Steinert worked as a nurse in several units, including labor and delivery, her daughter said. "She was just a little baby whisperer," Maggard said. "Children loved her." Maggard said she remembers music playing every time she went to her mom's house, and how her mom used to love dancing to country songs.
